spoken_transcript: Do not forcibly wake your child at 2 AM to administer flu medication. Oseltamivir, like Tamiflu, is typically taken twice daily, at 12-hour intervals. If the first day's dose timing must change, do not shorten the interval on your own; ask the prescriber or pharmacist. Sufficient sleep and rest are as crucial for flu recovery as the medication. If the first dose was at 2 PM, confirm the next dose time with the prescriber or pharmacist. Confirm the next day's dosing times as part of the full prescribed schedule. Starting medication within the first 48 hours inhibits viral replication most effectively. If your child vomits after oseltamivir, note when and how much, and ask a clinician or pharmacist before repeating a dose. Persistent high fever for 3 days, breathing difficulties, or worsening condition require medical attention. If symptoms worsen or other issues arise, consult your pediatrician without hesitation.
